chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said:

I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, it has been narrated from your fathers (peace be upon them) that for one who has intercourse or breaks his fast in the month of Ramadan, there are three expiations. And it has also been narrated from them that there is only one expiation. Which of the two reports should we follow?' He said: 'We take both. So whenever a man has unlawful intercourse or breaks his fast unlawfully in the month of Ramadan, he is obligated to three expiations: freeing a slave, fasting for two consecutive months, and feeding sixty poor people, plus making up that day. And if he had lawful intercourse or broke his fast lawfully, he is obligated to only one expiation.'

key_terms.كَفَّارَاتٍ: expiations (penalties for breaking a fast or committing a specific act)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in expiation for breaking the fast unlawfully versus lawfully in Ramadan according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) resolves the apparent contradiction in juristic reports by establishing that the severity of the expiation depends on the nature of the act: unlawful intercourse or breaking the fast intentionally incurs three cumulative expiations (freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, and feeding sixty poor), while lawful acts require only one. This ruling reflects the Shia principle of reconciling narrations by distinguishing between the gravity of the violation, emphasizing that intentional transgression against the sanctity of Ramadan demands a heavier penalty.
